Information since September points to a still-strong labor market and robust household spending, but persistent softness in business fixed investment and exports alongside below-target inflation and low market-based inflation compensation. Easing the policy rate and committing to ample reserves via T-bill purchases and repo operations is consistent with New Keynesian guidance to relax policy when inflation expectations are below target and output risks rise (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Svensson). The weakness in investment aligns with evidence that firms’ investment—especially inventories—is sensitive to internal funds and financial conditions (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994), which accommodative policy can partially offset. Empirical VAR results (Sims; Zha) support that such easing boosts real activity through interest-rate and liquidity channels. Overall tone: moderately dovish but cautious given uncertainties.
